answers.1a: Traditional n-gram language models suffer from a fixed context window limited to n-1 words (Markov assumption) and cannot capture long-range dependencies. Also suffers from sparsity when encountering unseen n-grams.
answers.1b: Transformers process all tokens in parallel using self-attention which is permutation-invariant and has no notion of word order. Positional encodings (sinusoidal encodings) are added to inject word order and position semantics.
answers.1c: Encoder-only architectures like BERT use bidirectional attention to learn representations for classification. Decoder-only architectures like GPT use causal autoregressive left-to-right attention for next-token generation.
answers.1d: Masked attention uses an upper-triangular mask matrix to prevent attention to future tokens during training, preventing information leakage during autoregressive generation.
answers.3a: Greedy decoding selects Word A with probability 0.4.
answers.3b: Top-2 candidate selection with k=2 yields Word A (0.4) and Word B (0.3).
answers.3c: Layer normalization is applied twice in each transformer block: once after multi-head attention to stabilize attention activations, and once after feed-forward network to stabilize representations and gradient flow across variable length sequences.
